My story

Why I do this work

People do their best work when they feel safe and trusted. Building that is why I do this.

  1. 01

    Safety was the first lesson

    I studied criminal justice and interned with a domestic violence unit. I learned law enforcement was not my path, but safety stayed with me. I saw how much a safe, trusting environment changes what people can do.

  2. 02

    Best Buy taught me engagement

    As a store manager I led teams on the floor and saw how much goes into keeping people engaged. I wanted to keep growing in corporate, where I could act on that passion at scale.

  3. 03

    HR is where I build it

    I moved into corporate HR at large brands, then startups, and built the People function at Ridecell over seven years. I want every employee I serve to have the best experience possible.

I let AI handle the routine work, with a person always reviewing it. That leaves more time for the conversations that matter.

How I work

From problem to proof

The pattern behind most of what I have built, in three steps.

Problems I get brought in to solve

  • HR infrastructure that cannot scale with the company
  • Compliance gaps that only show up at audit time
  • Manual payroll, leave, and approval processes
  • HRIS data that leaders do not trust
  • A People team that can only react

How I approach it

  • One source of truth in the HRIS, connected to payroll
  • Write it down: SOPs with named owners and backups
  • Automate the routine, keep a human where judgment matters
  • Controls and approvals that hold up in an audit
  • Coach managers and the team to run it themselves

What changes

  • HRIS to payroll sync from 1 to 2 days down to 2 to 3 hours
  • Six clean SOC 2 Type 2 audits in a row
  • 100% adoption of an approval workflow built with Claude
  • Leaders who trust their People data
  • A People team that works as a strategic partner

Case studies

How I work, in five stories

Five chapters, Ridecell first and then Prezent AI. Each one has a problem, a turn, an ending and a sequel.

Chapter I of V

People Operations built from zero

Ridecell | Dec 2018 - Jan 2026

The problem

Ridecell had no documentation beyond outdated files, headcount lived in spreadsheets, and there was no tracked channel for employee questions.

The turn

Built a 40+ procedure SOP library with named owners and backup coverage, ASKPeople (a Jira and Confluence ticketing system with tiered SLAs), and Sapling as the HR single source of truth, integrated with ADP and connected through Zapier.

How it ended

Supported the company across 3 to 5+ countries, 6 consecutive clean SOC 2 Type 2 audits, approval cycles cut from 1-2 days to 2-3 hours, and 5-10 tickets a day resolved within 24-48 hours.

Read the sequel: what I would do differently

I'd have started the SOP library and ticketing system in the first months. Documenting as I went would have been easier than catching up later.

SaplingADP Workforce NowJiraConfluenceZapier
Chapter II of V

A benefits renewal with one month to spare

Ridecell | Dec 2018 - Jan 2026

The problem

A re-rating moved the company from large group to small group one month before renewal.

The turn

Analyzed plans with the broker and switched carriers to Cigna, running a compressed open enrollment.

How it ended

Saved $30K a year with no coverage disruption.

Read the sequel: what I would do differently

I'd have checked the company's group-size status with the broker well before renewal, so the re-rating wouldn't have been a surprise.

Benefits renewalOpen enrollmentBroker partnership
Chapter III of V

One approval path for every HRIS change

Prezent AI | Feb 2026 - Apr 2026

The problem

HRIS changes ran through an undocumented, unapproved process, which created audit risk. Early on, some people felt a form would be too process-heavy.

The turn

Built a Claude-powered Employee Action Form requiring documentation and approval before any HRIS change, plus Notion New Hire and Offboarding workflows.

How it ended

100% adoption within one to two months, an audit trail that had not existed, and preboarding within 24 hours of offer acceptance.

Read the sequel: what I would do differently

I'd have piloted the form with one team first. Some people said it was too process-heavy, and early proof from a small group might have won them over faster.

ClaudeNotionRipplingSlack
Chapter IV of V

A reorganization with cost visibility

Prezent AI | Feb 2026 - Apr 2026

The problem

A reorganization affecting 15+ employees across the US and India needed severance, COBRA cost, and agreements prepared quickly and accurately.

The turn

Used AI-enabled severance and cost modeling (Claude and Gemini) that calculated severance, COBRA cost, and COBRA months owed and drafted agreements, tracked on a shared spreadsheet for Payroll and IT.

How it ended

First-time cost visibility for a reduction in force and agreement prep cut from 20 minutes per employee to about 3 hours total for the whole group.

Read the sequel: what I would do differently

I'd have built the cost model before the reorganization was decided. Leaders could then have compared scenarios rather than just seeing the cost of the chosen one.

ClaudeGeminiRipplingShared tracker
Chapter V of V

A C-suite search, filled in three weeks

Prezent AI | Feb 2026 - Apr 2026

The problem

A Chief Growth Officer search had 6 to 8 candidates in play and a three-week window.

The turn

Managed candidate travel, background checks, references and backdoor references, drafted the offer letter, and set up the new hire's onboarding experience, using Claude to automate candidate communications, interview scheduling, reference checks, and finalist travel.

How it ended

The role was filled in three weeks.

Read the sequel: what I would do differently

I'd lean more into AI and use it for the repetitive tasks. There was a lot to juggle across 6 to 8 candidates.

ClaudeWorkableScheduling automation

    30-60-90

    My first 90 days in a Director of People Operations role

    A starting point I would adapt after the first conversations with leadership and the team.

    Days 1 to 30

    Listen and map

    • Meet the executive team, the People team, and partners in Finance, Legal, and IT, and learn what is working and what hurts.
    • Audit the foundation: HRIS data quality, payroll accuracy, policies, the compliance calendar, and open employee cases.
    • Map the employee lifecycle end to end, with an owner and a handoff for every step.
    Days 31 to 60

    Design the first moves

    • Fix the highest-risk gaps first: data accuracy, approvals, and compliance deadlines.
    • Document the core workflows and stand up one tracked channel for employee questions.
    • Decide where automation helps and where human judgment has to stay.
    Days 61 to 90

    Ship and measure

    • Launch one automation on a real workflow, with a human review step.
    • Report turnaround time, data accuracy, and compliance status before and after.
    • Share a 12-month People Operations roadmap with leadership, built from what I learned.
    By month 6

    The outcome

    • Policies, systems, and data are documented, current, and audit-ready.
    • Managers and employees know where to go and get answers quickly.
    • More of the team's week goes to conversations and judgment calls, and less to manual work.

    Every company is different, so I would adjust this plan after listening to the executive team, the People team, and my partners in Finance, Legal, and IT.

    Beyond the resume

    How I found People Ops

    I realized my calling wasn't in the courtroom. It was in the workplace.
    1. Criminal Justice majorWanted to serve my community.
    2. Domestic violence unit internshipFound where I could do the most good.
    3. HR certificate, Los AngelesStudied while working.
    4. Retail, healthcare, Bay AreaLearned HR from every side.
    5. Startups, then RidecellSeven years, from Manager to Director.

    I care about People Ops as a craft. The systems, the process, and the compliance work matter because they give the people side of the job room to breathe: the hard conversation, the careful listening, the judgment call no tool can make. Outside work, I have a dog named Lizzy and a camera.

    Questions I get asked

    Quick answers

    Have you run a reduction in force?

    Yes. At Prezent AI I planned and ran one across the US and India for 15+ employees, with severance, COBRA, and agreements modeled and drafted using AI, plus a shared tracker for Payroll and IT. At Munchery I managed a WARN Act closure affecting a large group of employees. At Ridecell I supported the company through multiple reductions and restructurings with no compliance violations.

    Which HRIS and payroll systems have you used?

    Rippling, ADP Workforce Now, Kallidus Sapling, Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, UKG, PeopleSoft, and FinancialForce HCM. I led the Sapling implementation and integrated it with ADP, which cut approval turnaround from 1 to 2 days to 2 to 3 hours.

    How do you use AI in People Ops?

    For the routine work, with a human reviewing anything that needs judgment. I built a Claude-powered Employee Action Form that reached 100% adoption and created an audit trail that did not exist before. I also built severance and cost models, and automations with Zapier and n8n.

    How do you handle compliance in more than one country?

    I build the program once and adapt it by jurisdiction: I-9, FLSA, GDPR, and CCPA, plus Employer of Record setups in Canada, the UK, and Dubai. I have partnered with five outside immigration counsels, and the audit record is six clean SOC 2 Type 2 audits in a row.

    Have you only worked at startups?

    No. I started at large corporations: Quiksilver/Roxy/DC, VF Corporation (Lucy and The North Face), and Dolby. That is where I learned process, compliance, and scale. I then moved to startups on purpose, to grow faster and own more, first at Munchery and then at Ridecell, where I built the People function and kept 90% of the employees I took on during the 2019 scaling for 5+ years.

    Why did you leave Prezent AI?

    The team was in India and I was in the US, and the time zone gap made the role unsustainable for me long term. I am looking for a role where my hours overlap with my team and leaders, EST to PST. At Prezent I still ran a 60-day audit, an acquisition integration, and a reorganization, and I led a team of 8 that I restructured to 6 and grew back to 7.

    What size team have you led?

    At Ridecell, 2 direct reports plus 2 dotted-line recruiters, while owning People Operations for 350+ employees. At Prezent AI, an India-based team of 8, restructured to 6 and then 7.

    Are you more strategic or hands-on?

    Both, and I think a first People leader has to be. I wrote the SOP library, and I also personally onboarded and offboarded every Ridecell employee.

    What would your first 30 days look like?

    Listening and mapping. I would meet the executive team, the People team, and partners in Finance, Legal, and IT to learn what is working, then document the current state before changing anything. The full 30-60-90 plan is further down the page.

    How do you work with managers?

    I give them tools and early involvement rather than rules after the fact. That meant a manager toolkit, early HR involvement before any termination, and an offboarding process that moved our Glassdoor rating from 3.6 to 3.9.
